title: What if the harness mattered more than the model? - Aditya Bhargava, Etsy
talk_summary: Aditya Bhargava (Etsy) argues the harness (everything around the model) can matter more than the model, citing HarnessBench where identical models scored 52.4%–76.2% across harnesses, with weaker models benefiting most. He demos a coding agent in his 'Agency' language evolving through seven harness improvements: tools, safety interrupts/handlers, partial function application for sandboxing, ReAct feedback loops, sub-agents as tools, and prompt self-optimization.

takeaways.technique: Sub-agents as tools to cut context bloat
takeaways.what_they_do: Top-level agent gets sub-agents (coding agent, Wikipedia agent) as its only tools; each sub-agent has its own LLM call, system prompt, and scoped toolset, so unrelated tools never pollute the parent's context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sub agents are cool because they let you add new capabilities without bloating context

takeaways.technique: Partial function application to lock tool arguments
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of human approval on every file read/write, they bind the directory argument at tool-construction time so the LLM never sees or controls it; the agent is autonomous but can only touch the allowed directory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're locking the directory argument to demo. Um the LLM isn't going to be able to change that argument

takeaways.technique: ReAct loop gated on test pass/fail
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent prompt requires reason→act→observe: read files, run tests, read failure, edit, rerun until tests pass, rather than proposing a fix and stopping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: reason, read the two files, act, run the tests, observe, if the tests fail, read the error, and then reason again

takeaways.technique: Automated prompt optimization against a measurable objective
takeaways.what_they_do: Mark prompt variables with an 'optimize' modifier, give the optimizer a goal and a baseline score, and it rewrites prompts iteratively, measuring each candidate instead of hand-tuning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not guessing and checking. We're systematically measuring and improving
takeaways.numbers: baseline objective 0.2; optimizer hit the objective in the first iteration in the demo

takeaways.technique: Harness investment as a substitute for expensive models
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that because harness quality disproportionately helps weaker models, a strong harness lets you run open/local models and still hit cutting-edge performance, reducing dependence on paid proprietary models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for weaker models, the harness matters more
takeaways.numbers: HarnessBench: same model, different harnesses scored 52.4% to 76.2% (>20-point spread)

takeaways.what_they_do: Interrupts pause execution at the exact point (inside a loop, tool call, or sub-agent), serialize state, and resume later without code changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can serialize the execution, you can come back to it a week later, and you don't need to change anything
